name: TX-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: Weber's large financial advantage ($972K raised vs $27K, Bartie in the red)
No polls or expert ratings; markets price Weber near 95%
model.rationale: Weber holds a heavily Republican Gulf Coast seat with a decisive money edge and no meaningful outside spending against him, while Bartie has raised almost nothing and is out of cash. Markets price Weber's win odds around 95%, consistent with the district's fundamentals.
model.watch: A late Democratic outside-spending surge or a major Weber scandal could narrow the race, but neither is currently in evidence.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Randy Weber seeks another term in this Republican-leaning Southeast Texas district, where the partisan lean favors the GOP by double digits. He enters the general election with a well-funded campaign, nearly $920,000 on hand, and no outside groups opposing him.

Challenger Thurman Bartie has raised only about $27,000 and reports negative cash on hand, leaving him little capacity to compete. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Weber roughly a 95% chance of winning. The forecast places this race firmly in the Safe Republican column, with the main uncertainty being the usual range of error in a low-information contest.
